memos.scout:
I can't make a strong case for buying this one. The brief shows a coin that has already lost most of its value: down 76% over 30 minutes, down 87% over the last 15 minutes, and sitting 90% below its 30-minute high. Net flow over the last 15 minutes was negative (-60 SOL), with 696 SOL sold against 636 SOL bought and more sellers (1,216) than buyers (1,417) in that window. Sell-to-buy ratio in the first two minutes after graduation was 0.97, meaning early buyers were already exiting almost as fast as they entered.

The only mildly positive signals are that the top-3 holder share is low (6.5%), the top-5 buyer share is modest (13%), and it's classed ORGANIC with no airdrop dump seen. Those point to a broad holder base, but they don't show demand that will persist. A broad base of holders who are selling into a collapse is not evidence of demand that holds for the next 30-60 minutes. The bundle share (33%) and launch bot presence also warrant caution.

Against a base rate of roughly -20% per trade for random post-graduation buys, plus 1.4-5.1% round-trip costs, and a chart that is in an active collapse, the honest scout call is to skip. A skipped coin costs nothing.
memos.skeptic: The most likely loss path is distribution into the rebound. The coin is already down 89.8% from its 30-minute high and 86.8% over the last 15 minutes, with net flow of -60.25 SOL and sells (696 SOL) outpacing buys (636 SOL). The last-15-minute sell-to-buy ratio is above 1, and 1,216 sellers against 1,417 buyers means holders are exiting, not accumulating. The launch-bot flag and a 0.97 sell-to-buy ratio in the first two minutes after graduation point to early snipers flipping. With a 42.9 SOL pool, a $20 round trip faces 1.4-5.1% costs, and a 30-second execution lag means any bounce gets sold into by the same flow. A dead-cat bounce is the likely trap, not a reversal. Pass.
